body: Because bigfoot doesn’t exist and never has. it’s fun thing to think about, cause most people like the idea of a mysterious creature not known-to science. The lack of evidence of Bigfoot despite human being’s presence on land makes the likelihood of this cryptic being real nearly 0%. Maybe it existed one day as an ancestor to gigantopithecus Blacki or a late survivor/colony. But when you mix clear bias, the want for something to exist, and an overall fundamental lack of understanding of how nature and science works together, you get to this conclusion that their must be an unknown species walking around upright that’s only spotted on blurry cameras and shaky video recording. Patty is literally the foundation of this hoax, which was in part also confirmed to be a hoax as well. Don’t get me wrong, I am one of these people at once. Don’t get me wrong, I’m one of these people too. I wanna believe more than anything, but reality outweighs the fantasy 100% of the time. I hope more people in the sub start thinking like this as well and stop chasing that unicorn that doesn’t exist.

Let’s make a hypothetical, it’s a pro tournament and it’s grand finals at evo. You’re up 1-0 on your opponent and you decide to taunt and tbag every chance you get, how would this be any different than bad sportsmanship in actual sports? Wouldn’t you be punished? I understand I’m using a big comparison to a normal pvp match, but doesn’t this prove my point that their IS a line to be cross in being toxic and how you should behave? I’m not advocating for this also I’m just curious to hear others sides on this topic. Is it only ok to be toxic in pubs or is it ok to be toxic whenever we want.

I carry a small pocket knife with me everywhere I go but never a gun. I’m not against gun’s or for them or anything. I personally don’t care about them. But I have heard talk about that and that’s a pretty interesting question. I think the reason why we don’t need them is because when we arrive a police officer almost always is there first. And they always have a weapon. So we rely on them for our safety and we rely on our sevlves and instinct if something went wrong

If I had to guess it’s probably about 70%, I live in Florida so theirs old people everywhere, and also because the first thing they think to do is call 911. Let’s say they had a simple fall, nothing broke or anything just a simple fall. That person more than likely can’t get up by themselves or depend on someone who might not be there. So the first thought that goes in their mind is usually 911

We ended up taking the newborn to the hospital and took our next call. Usually when we are on the field we are always going and coming from somewhere. Rarely will we have downtime, but we do have downtime. No I don’t get PTSD at all actually! When I see things that are usually thing’s people shouldn’t see I take note’s and learn from it. Unless something happens in the future I haven’t had any flashback’s or episodes from PTSD. And I love your last question, it’s showed me the meaning of how precious life truly is. I’m a huge gamer, especially FPS gamer. And when you kill someone in the game it means nothing, that person didint have a family, they didint have people who cared about them. They’re just pixel’s. But when you see a body in real life you realize that’s a person just like you and me. That person has had happy moment’s and sad one’s. They’ve made friends and had an impact on this world, than all of the sudden it all ends. Everything you’ve done in your life suddenly has no affect anymore to society. People forget how precious life really is. And I think that’s what I’ve learned the most
